about: Mutants of the fuzz-core self-test (run.sh --selftest). Each patch is a unified diff against the KenseiECS package folder; it is applied to a copy of the tree under test, never to the tree itself. kind bug: an injected defect, which the module must report as a new signature (family NEW, not absorbed into a known family) with a repro that reproduces. kind fix: an emulated correction of a known family, which must make that family disappear without any new signature (no false positive on corrected behaviour). kind regression: a change where the contract is silent, which must come out as status regression, not as a defect. kind out-of-scope: listed for completeness, not run. A bug mutant is killed only by a new signature of family NEW, with a reproducing repro, whose rule starts with one of its 'match' rules and whose mechanism facts contain that entry's fact (the mechanism it was written for); new signatures of other rules are KILLED-OTHER, a bug mutant without 'match' is UNSPECIFIED: both fail the self-test.

mutants.name: nov-debug-stale-reused-passes
mutants.origin: completeness critique: same class as W6 in a new place
mutants.what: ValidateHandle ignores the generation: under KENSEI_DEBUG a stale handle whose slot was reused passes Add/Get/Has/Remove/AddEvent and acts on the new occupant
mutants.expect: X-missing-throw with fact stale-accepted:reused+idle, not W6 (W6 is a free slot while a DestroyEntity is in progress)

mutants.name: nov-copy-dead-leaks-entity
mutants.origin: completeness critique: side effect before the check (G1 class)
mutants.what: CopyEntity creates the copy before checking the source: a dead source leaks an alive entity without components
mutants.expect: R-alive-empty@copy with fact copy-src-dead, not N3 (N3 copies an alive source inside the removal of its last component)
mutants.version_note: the 2.2.1 CopyEntity; nov-copy-dead-leaks-entity-222 is the same mutant for the 2.2.2 code

mutants.name: nov-group-claims-pools
mutants.origin: completeness critique (M1): side effect before the check, new place World.RegisterGroup
mutants.what: RegisterGroup checks and claims the pools in one pass: a Group<C, B>() rejected because B belongs to Group<A, B> leaves C owned by an unregistered group, which reorders the dense array of B when C is added (Group<A, B> loses its alignment) and makes a later Group<C, D>() throw
mutants.expect: R-group (alignment or membership of the existing group) after a rejected registration, or X-unexpected-throw of a later group over the freed type (the model registers it: fact group-new)

mutants.name: nov-world-compadded-live-array
mutants.origin: completeness critique (M2): listener reentrancy, new place IWorldEventListener.OnComponentAdded
mutants.what: The OnComponentAdded dispatch walks the live listener array instead of the one captured at its start: a listener that unsubscribes itself makes the next one miss the event, one subscribed during the dispatch gets it at once
mutants.expect: N-missing or N-extra:world-compAdded with fact listeners-changed:world (a world listener changed the listener set during the dispatch)

mutants.expect: N-missing or N-extra:filter-leave with fact listeners-changed:filter

mutants.name: rev-typed-added-early-capture-222
mutants.version_note: rolls back a fix of the 2.2.2 code itself (the OnAdded dispatch takes the typed listeners after the world update)

mutants.name: nov-eventbuffer-other-holder-222
mutants.version_note: the list holder that 2.2.2 records (EventBuffer XML doc: a pooled list is held by one entity at most)
mutants.origin: the W5 class (one pooled list on two entities) in a new place: a copy of another entity's EventBuffer stored for this one
mutants.what: Storing an EventBuffer value no longer checks which entity holds its list: a copy of another entity's buffer stored through Add or CommandBuffer.Set shares that entity's list
mutants.expect: an ownership, value or payload failure with the fact cross-copy-store (a copy of another entity's buffer stored for this one), not W5 (W5 is a stale copy)

mutants.name: fix-w6-dying-slot-only
mutants.origin: emulated correction of W6 (a check of the model, not a proposal for the package)
mutants.what: While a DestroyEntity is in progress, a dead handle is accepted only for a slot that is not free (the entity being destroyed)
mutants.expect: W6 disappears and no new signature appears
mutants.version_note: 2.2.2 fixed W6 itself (a dead handle is accepted only for the entity being destroyed): the base run is that check there

mutants.name: fix-w1-warmup-stops

mutants.expect: W1 disappears and no new signature appears
mutants.version_note: 2.2.2 fixed W1 its own way (Warmup goes on with a new temporary entity): the base run is that check there

mutants.name: reg-created-after-death-skipped
mutants.origin: emulated change of contract-silent behaviour (a check of the regression status)
mutants.what: CreateEntity and CopyEntity no longer send OnEntityCreated for an entity a listener destroyed during its own creation (the contract does not say whether they should: question Q-created-after-death)
mutants.expect: new signatures only with status regression (the alternative reading of Q-created-after-death explains them), no new defect
mutants.version_note: 2.2.2 documents this very behaviour (claim created-alive-only): there it is the contract, not a contract-silent change
